newsitem.title: SLOVENIA: Istrabenz plans to pay first dividend.
newsitem.headline: Istrabenz plans to pay first dividend.

text.p: Slovenian petrol trading company Istrabenz said on Wednesday it planned to pay a dividend for the first time for 1996 and that it would total 50 tolars ($0.3) per share.

"We decided to pay a dividend after negotiations with major shareholders although the management earlier suggested not to pay one in order to invest as much as possible," Srecko Kenda, Istrabenz's deputy executive for finances, told Reuters.
The company said the payout still needs shareholder approval, which is expected at the end of May.

Istrabenz, 18-percent owned by Austria's largest industrial group OMV and 13.3 percent by the Slovenian state, said it expects sales to grow over 10 percent in 1997 due to a 9.5 percent increase of petrol prices at the end of March.
Profits are also expected to improve, but Kenda added the level of growth largely depended upon the government's policy regarding petrol prices.

Group 1996 net profit fell to 271.4 million tolars ($1.7 million) from 1.4 billion in 1995 as a result of low petrol prices, while sales rose to 32.4 billion tolars from 24.4 billion. -- Marja Novak, Ljubljana newsroom, 386-61-125-8439
